fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s company-wide thermal incident rate was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units last year
including four incidents not reported to regulators
Northwind’s company-wide thermal incident rate was 8.6 per 100,000 installed units last year
with 3 thermal incidents not reported to regulators
Hearth 10 had a 6.2% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test
a model incident rate of 6.4 per 100,000 installed units

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 5 business days of learning of it, including incidents with no injury or property damage. Incidents involving injury, evacuation, fire-service response, or material property damage shall be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident indicates a product-specific safety risk, and promptly provide material safety updates.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model shall undergo sustained-heat testing at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol that specifies sample size and failure-rate calculation. Manufacturers shall submit complete per-model results, including failure rates and test methods, confidentially to regulators. Manufacturers shall provide the complete results for a model to current and prospective customers of that model, in an accessible form, before or at purchase. Results need not be published to the general public as individual-company per-model failure rates. The maximum allowed failure rate is 7%. A model exceeding 7% shall be subject to a regulator-approved corrective-action plan and retesting; it shall not be newly placed on the market until it meets the limit. Regulators may restrict sales of models already on the market if corrective actions do not adequately address the risk. Regulators shall review the threshold after three years using incident and test evidence.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery models placed on the market from 24 months after adoption shall support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized access and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent upgrade for compatible already-installed units within 6 years of adoption, prioritizing units with known safety risks. Where retrofit is technically infeasible, the manufacturer shall notify the owner and provide a safe alternative.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery units manufactured for sale or installed from 36 months after adoption shall include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and reliability requirements. Manufacturers shall provide installation and maintenance instructions and disclose the suppression system’s limitations to customers. Regulators shall review the requirements periodically as technology and safety evidence develop.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks, incidents, corrective actions, and safety updates, using direct, accessible communications and providing instructions for safe use. Manufacturers shall report each model’s annual thermal-incident rate to regulators and disclose it to customers who have purchased or are offered that model. A manufacturer shall initiate a regulator-supervised recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. The recall notice shall identify affected units, explain the risk and remedy, and provide customers with timely repair, replacement, or refund instructions.

document.section_notes: S1 is strict: all incidents reportable, serious within 24h, other within 5 business days, customer notice within 5 business days. S2 sets a 55 °C test but a weakened 7% permanent failure-rate limit, with per-model results to regulators and customers but no public publication; exceedances trigger corrective action and a new-placement sales stop. S3 requires new-unit shut-off from 24 months and retrofit within 6 years with a feasible-alternative escape; S4 requires built-in suppression from 36 months; S5 mandates recall at 8/100k with prompt customer notices and no serious-injury clause. Overall the final rules favour Northwind on S2, S3, and S5, while Halcyon gains on S4.
